objective: Align the local Cloud IaC app OpenTofu module-registry download response with repo-local protocol fixtures by returning /artifacts/modules/<archive>.zip locations and serving local deterministic archive bytes from the filesystem when present, without claiming object-store serving, production authentication, deployed endpoints, registry publish, provider runtime, FD-001 tenant workload hosting, or cloud provisioning.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: OpenTofu service discovery uses /.well-known/terraform.json and service identifiers such as modules.v1.
The module registry download endpoint returns a JSON location or X-Terraform-Get header; relative locations beginning with / are valid.
HTTP archive URLs ending in common archive extensions such as .zip are valid module sources for module installation.

implemented_claims: Broadened OpenTofu module release source validation to accept safe /artifacts/modules/<archive>-<version>.zip relative archive locations while preserving existing exact git ref validation.
Extended the app release-index loader to parse and validate archive_file and archive_media_type fields.
Changed release-index-backed app registry releases to return /artifacts/modules/<archive>.zip download locations matching repo-local protocol fixtures.
Registered a local /artifacts/modules/{archive_file} app route that serves bytes from target/oya-cloud-iac/module-archives when the deterministic archive file exists.
Updated manifest, catalog, tasks, evidence, and audit-chain scope with truthful local filesystem artifact-serving claims and nonclaims.
Hardened app tests so secret-like release-index evidence rejection is exercised after required archive fields are present, avoiding a false-positive test path.
Added artifact-route fail-closed coverage for invalid archive request names, unknown configured artifacts, and missing local archive files.
explicit_non_claims: no database adapter or persistent registry store
no production authentication runtime or Cedar runtime integration
no signed module releases, Sigstore/cosign execution, SLSA, or VSA attestation generation
no provider runtime, provider API calls, provider credentials, or cloud provisioning
no live Argo CD rollout, Kubernetes rollout, or Jenkins pipeline execution
no measured SLO, DR, sharding execution, tenant migration, or capacity telemetry
no FD-001 microservice dogfood tenant workload hosting or production tenant evidence
no aggregate ./bin/oya gate run-all success claim for current worktree
false_green_findings_closed: Repo-local protocol fixtures used /artifacts/modules/*.zip locations while the app returned git:: source URLs for release-index-backed downloads; app download responses now use artifact locations derived from archive_file metadata.
A relative artifact location previously had no app route to retrieve local archive bytes; the app now has a local filesystem route for deterministic archive files when present.
The app still does not claim object storage or production endpoint readiness; the new route is explicitly local filesystem only.

A release-index negative test was passing before reaching the secret-like evidence check because newly required archive fields were absent; the test fixture now includes archive_file and archive_media_type before asserting the evidence rejection.
Artifact route error behavior is now covered for invalid, unknown, and missing local archive requests rather than inferred from implementation only.
known_gaps: The local artifact route reads files from target/oya-cloud-iac/module-archives; production object-store-backed serving remains future work.
Runtime/API tests that construct releases manually still cover git:: source locations; release-index-backed app tests cover artifact locations.
Production authentication, persistence, signed releases, OpenTofu plan/apply, provider runtime, and live GitOps/Kubernetes rollout evidence remain future work.
FD-001 remains the product delivery goal; this ChangeSet is substrate progress only and does not prove FD-001 tenant workload hosting.
Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required and aggregate gate run-all are not claimed by this Cloud IaC slice.

findings: Kept the slice direct: safe relative archive source validation, archive metadata parsing, artifact location derivation, and one local file-serving route.
Closes a protocol/app mismatch on the module download path, a prerequisite for later private registry dogfood and FD-001 tenant workload hosting.
RED captured both missing domain support and missing app artifact route. GREEN tests include positive artifact serving and negative unpinned/traversal archive source cases.
Self-review found and fixed a negative-test false-positive path; post-review tests now assert the intended secret-like evidence rejection and artifact route fail-closed responses.
Download JSON now points to the same /artifacts/modules path shape already present in protocol fixtures, reducing local operator surprise.
Focused app/domain tests are green before broader final gates; final scoped gates are recorded separately.
Post-review test hardening added request-time 400/404 artifact-route coverage and all scoped Rust/gate validations were rerun.

rejected_reasons: Keeping git:: URLs preserves fixture/app divergence.
Object-store serving would overreach current local-foundation scope and require credentials/runtime surfaces not yet claimed.

findings: Archive source, archive_file, request filename, and evidence fields reject traversal or credential-like markers; artifact route maps only prevalidated archive filenames.
The app route rejects unsafe requested archive names before filesystem reads and serves only configured prevalidated archive basenames.
Local route reads archive bytes into memory for foundation-sized deterministic ZIPs only; no throughput/SLO claim is made.
Manifest/catalog/task evidence records local scope and nonclaims; no compliance certification or production rollout is claimed.
OpenTofu registry download JSON remains a location response; release-index-backed location now uses a relative archive path allowed by official protocol docs.
App startup validates archive metadata; artifact route fails closed with 404 when a configured local archive file is absent.
ChangeSet is tied to Oya VCS claim, manifest IP/capability row, catalog record, tasks, evidence bundle, and audit-chain closeout row.
Used Oya VCS claim; avoided raw git/gh; read root-hub and docs/AGENTS; kept /plan complementary-only; did not claim production/hyperscaler completion.
No new external dependencies were introduced; artifact serving uses std filesystem reads plus existing router/runtime boundaries.

review_findings_closed: Release-index secret-like-evidence negative fixture now includes required archive fields so it tests the intended condition.
App route fail-closed behavior for invalid, unknown, and missing artifact requests is covered by integration tests.
App top-level nonclaim was clarified from module-object storage to production object storage so the new local filesystem seam is not contradicted.
